subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the equation of locus of a point, the sum of whose distances from (0,2) and (0,−2) is 6 units.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what you would do before squaring, and name the shape the locus turns out to be.

steps.label: Take the locus point
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own. Both fixed points sit on the y-axis, so the x-terms will cancel in the same way as its partner question.
lines: Let P = (x, y) be a point on the locus.

recall.must_convey: That the moving point is named P = (x, y) and the fixed points are written down.
accept: let P be x comma y
take the locus point as P x y
P equals x comma y is on the locus
locus point ni P x y ga teesukovali
name the moving point P with coordinates x and y

steps.why: Every locus question starts the same way: the moving point gets coordinates, and the condition is then written in terms of those coordinates.
common_mistakes: Giving the moving point fixed numbers instead of (x, y).
Mixing up which points are fixed and which one moves.

steps.label: Write the given condition
steps.margin_note: First mark. Isolate one distance, then square — never square a sum of two roots directly.

recall.must_convey: That PA is isolated as 6 − PB and squared, giving 12PB = 36 + PB² − PA².
accept: shift P B across and square to get thirty six plus P B squared minus twelve P B
isolate one distance first then square both sides
write P A as six minus P B and square it
oka distance separate chesi square cheyyali
rearrange to get twelve P B on one side

steps.why: A sum of two distances cannot be squared directly — squaring PA + PB gives a cross term. Isolating one distance first is what keeps the algebra finite.
common_mistakes: Squaring PA + PB = 6 directly and being left with a cross term.

steps.label: Substitute the distances
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Both fixed points have x = 0, so the x² terms are identical and cancel, and a difference of two squares in y finishes the line.

recall.must_convey: That the x² terms cancel and the difference of squares gives 3PB = 9 + 2y.
accept: the x squared terms cancel and the y difference of squares gives four a b
substitute and use a plus b whole squared minus a minus b whole squared equals four a b
both x terms are the same so they cancel leaving three P B equals nine plus two y
x terms cancel avuthaayi, y lo difference of squares
reduce it to three P B equals nine plus two y

steps.why: PA² − PB² is a difference of two squares, so the y-terms collapse by (a+b)² − (a−b)² = 4ab and the whole line drops to the first degree.
common_mistakes: Expanding both y-brackets fully and slipping a sign instead of cancelling.
Taking 4ab as 4(2)(y) but writing 8y² instead of 8y.

steps.label: Simplify to the locus
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. The 36y cancels across, 9y² − 4y² leaves 5y², and the constants give 45. Unequal positive coefficients again — an ellipse.

recall.must_convey: That squaring again and collecting gives 9x² + 5y² = 45.
accept: square again and collect to get nine x squared plus five y squared equals forty five
the thirty six y cancels and nine y squared minus four y squared is five y squared
square both sides once more and simplify to the ellipse
malli square chesi simplify chesthe nine x square plus five y square equals forty five
the locus is an ellipse

steps.why: The locus of a point whose distances to two fixed points add to a constant is an ellipse with those points as foci, so unequal positive coefficients on x² and y² are the expected finish.
common_mistakes: Forgetting that 36y appears on both sides and cancels.
Multiplying only x² by 9 and leaving the y-bracket alone.
